Pete Sampras. An American tennis champion who dominated the nineteen nineties with fourteen Grand Slam singles titles. Between nineteen ninety and two thousand and two, he held the all-time record for most Grand Slams until Roger Federer surpassed him twelve years after his retirement.

Sampras was a grass-court specialist, and his seven Wimbledon titles were the cornerstone of his career. His powerful serve was devastatingly effective on fast surfaces, making Wimbledon his signature tournament. While he won the Australian Open, US Open, and French Open once each, his consistency at Wimbledon set him apart as one of the greatest players ever on grass.

In nineteen ninety-three, Sampras reached the world number one ranking and held that position for a then-record two hundred eighty-six weeks. His breakthrough was marked by notable victories: he defeated Andre Agassi in the nineteen ninety US Open final and Ivan Lendl in the nineteen ninety-two US Open.

Sampras retired in two thousand and two while still ranked in the top ten, which was unusual for his era. He later married fellow tennis player Bridgette Wilson. As the modern predecessor to Federer, Sampras embodied American tennis excellence in the era before the Roger Federer dominance that would follow.
